summary: Branch mesh AP ARP suppression + client-isolation causing intermittent internal service discovery timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers in the SF branch reported intermittent timeouts when hitting internal K8s API services (team dashboards, CI runners) over corporate Wi‑Fi. Impact: Affected team members experienced 10–30s timeouts or 502/504 errors against internal services intermittently during the day. Scope: ~10–25% of clients on the branch mesh; not global.

Observed behavior: Client HTTP/gRPC calls to internal services would hang for ~15–25s then either succeed or return a 504. Simultaneously, packet captures from affected clients showed ARP requests for service VIPs with no ARP reply from the AP/edge for extended periods. When the same client switched to wired network or another site, issues disappeared.

Expected behavior: Mesh APs should proxy/forward ARP and not suppress legitimate ARP requests for internal VIPs. Service discovery and routing should remain stable during client roaming between mesh nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect corporate laptop to branch mesh SSID (ssid: redwood-office).
2) Start continuous curl -v against internal k8s service VIP (https://svc-internal.redwood.local:8443).
3) Walk across open office to trigger mesh roaming between APs (or force disconnect via AP web UI).
4) Observe intermittent large request latencies (15-25s) or HTTP 502/504 failures.
logs: WiFi AP syslog (excerpt): [Mar 05 09:13:12] AP-03 client-steer: suppress-arp for 10.18.3.45 -> 10.18.0.200; [Mar 05 09:13:13] AP-01 client-assoc: sta 02:12:ab:cd:ef:01 roam->AP-03; Edge firewall logs show NAT-translation hits but no ARP proxy reply during suppression windows.
investigation_notes: 10:22 - Triage: Collected pcap from affected client and APs (AP-01 and AP-03). Noted ARP requests for cluster VIP (10.18.0.200) with repeated retransmits; AP forwarded some ARP replies but often dropped them during 'suppression' windows.

11:05 - Hypothesis: Mesh controller feature 'ARP suppression / proxy' (enabled to reduce broadcast storms) is aggressively suppressing/proxying ARPs but has a bug where it suppresses ARPs while the client attachment state is still transitioning (roaming edge-case).

11:30 - Reproduced: Forced roaming between AP-01->AP-03 while running tcpdump on AP-03. Observed ARP suppression log entries coincident with client reassociation; these windows match user-visible timeouts to k8s services.

12:10 - Correlation: Only clients that relied on internal VIPs (k8s services) and had short-lived sticky sessions were impacted. DNS lookups succeeded; TCP handshakes stalled waiting for ARP resolution, hence HTTP timeouts rather than DNS failures.
13:00 - Check config: Mesh firmware 5.4.2 has 'arp_proxy_aggressive=true' set at site profile. Vendor release notes show a related bug fixed in 5.5.0 where proxy incorrectly drops ARP during roam.
13:45 - Communication: Opened fast-track with WiFi vendor TAC (case #TAC-2026-143) and linked AP syslogs and pcaps.
comments: Maya Chen (reporter) [2026-03-05 10:00]: Users started reporting intermittent timeouts after morning standups. Filing ticket to collect traces.

SRE Oncall - Priya Patel [2026-03-05 11:40]: Collected tcpdumps, seeing repeated ARP requests from clients for 10.18.0.200 with no reply during the timeout window. Moving to investigate mesh AP behaviour.

WiFi Eng - Alex Nguyen [2026-03-05 12:30]: Confirmed 'arp_proxy_aggressive' set on site profile. Vendor notes suggest issue in 5.4.x series during fast roam. Recommending temporary disable of 'ARP suppression' as mitigation.
Diego Alvarez (assignee) [2026-03-05 13:20]: Will put change in place during 16:00 maintenance window. Will monitor for regressions and vendor response.
Vendor TAC [2026-03-05 15:10]: Acknowledged bug, provided hotfix image 5.4.2-hf1 that addresses suppression race during roam. Recommended either apply hotfix or disable feature as workaround.
Diego Alvarez [2026-03-05 16:30]: Rolled back 'arp_proxy_aggressive' to false on branch site profile during maintenance window. Applied vendor hotfix to AP-03 (root) for additional validation.
resolution:
Root cause: Mesh controller's aggressive ARP suppression/proxy feature incorrectly suppressed ARP replies during fast client roaming windows, causing clients to fail to resolve cluster VIPs and producing 15-25s application timeouts.

Mitigation and fix deployed: 1) Disabled 'arp_proxy_aggressive' on branch site profile (immediate mitigation). 2) Applied vendor hotfix 5.4.2-hf1 to root AP and staged roll to satellite APs (completed 2026-03-06). 3) Adjusted AP roaming thresholds (lowered roam hysteresis) and increased ARP proxy fallback timers.

Verification: Post-change monitoring across 72 hours showed dropped error rates to baseline (internal service 5xxs returned to <0.5% at the site) and user reports ceased. PCAP samples show ARP replies delivered promptly during roam.

Follow-ups / Action items: [2026-03-09] - WiFi Eng to schedule full-site hotfix rollout and perform customer-style acceptance testing. [2026-03-09] - Update runbook for branch mesh profiles to include 'disable aggressive ARP proxy' as a temporary troubleshooting step for service discovery timeouts. [2026-03-12] - Postmortem page: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/INT-657890-mesh-arp-suppression-postmortem
